To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the manufacturing ‘small’ sector is not well developed; (2) low demand for goods is the overriding factor that constrains access to market; (3) low demand is caused by a combination of factors including low purchasing power of the populace, low level of economic activities in the area, low level of technology, and low quality of goods; and (4) the government has a critical role to play in the growth of the manufacturing sector.
the two most relevant binding constraint identified by the manufacturing ‘small’ sector in Ghana are limited access to technology and limited access to market.

(1) the most important constraint to access of market by the manufacturing ‘small’ enterprises in the study area is lack of demand for goods; and (2) the most important factor contributing to the lack of demand is low purchasing power of the populace.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the manufacturing sector of small businesses in Ghana is able to access markets.
the extent to which a manufacturing ‘small business’ sector is able to access market.
the extent of access to market of manufacturing small businesses in Ghana, the factors that constrain their ability to access market and how to tackle those constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the manufacturing sector of the Ghanaian economy is in a state of underdevelopment.
the overriding binding constraint of limited access of the manufacturing small business sector in Ghana to market was low demand for goods.
the manufacturing ‘small’ enterprise sector is not yet ready for the market, but is rather still in the process of learning and self-discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the manufacturing small businesses sector in Ghana is faced with a number of binding constraints, but the most overriding one is limited access to market.
, in the absence of a national vision and co-ordinated efforts by all stakeholders, it is difficult for manufacturing ‘small’ firms to grow and contribute to the development of the country.
the government needs to take a more proactive role in the development of the manufacturing ‘small’ enterprise sector in Ghana.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the government should be the champion of self-discovery of the nation, and the creation of required co–ordination externalities.
, in the absence of a well-functioning market, it is imperative for government to play a role in creating market.
, the manufacturing small business sector in Ghana is not a homogeneous sector.
